headline: down to $0.074, its lowest since December 2025, while CapConnect+ joins the Super Validators
lede: Canton Coin (CC) price, chart levels and three scenarios for the week ahead, plus what's happening with CNTN stock. Plain English, no hype.
summary: Canton Coin is at $0.0736 (about R1.30), down about 8% this week and 29% this month. Last week's $0.075 support gave way on 20 November and CC touched about $0.071, its lowest since mid December 2025. The whole market is still in Extreme Fear (index at 11), and Bitcoin and Ether both fell about 9% over 7 days. On the network side, CapConnect+ was approved as a Super Validator on 18 November, Talos, Marex and Broadridge announced plans for tokenized Treasury financing on Canton, and the first technical plan for universal burn (CIP-0132) was proposed. CNTN stock fell about 29% to $1.21, a new 52 week low, despite its first positive adjusted EBITDA quarter.

changed: 📉 Price went from $0.0801 to $0.0736, about 8% lower. There was a bounce to about $0.087 on 16 November, then sellers took over again.
🧱 Last week's $0.075 support broke on 20 November. CC touched about $0.071 on Kraken on 21 November, the lowest since mid December 2025.
🌍 Still a market-wide mood: Bitcoin and Ether both fell about 9% in 7 days, and the Fear and Greed Index has stayed between 10 and 12 all week.
🏛️ CapConnect+ was approved as a Super Validator on 18 November (CIP-0131), one week after Nomura.
📉 CNTN stock fell from $1.71 to $1.21 (about -29%), a new 52 week low, even though its third quarter showed its first positive adjusted EBITDA.
technicals: Down: lower highs since February, and another lower low this week
About 30: still near oversold, but not as stretched as the price drop suggests (the falls are getting smaller)
Below its signal line and below zero, the gap still slightly widening (bearish)
Fading: from about $17 to $18 million a day on 15 and 16 November to about $7 to $8 million now. Quieter selling, not heavy panic
At least $24 million open interest across the 11 biggest venues checked (Binance about $9.7 million, Bybit about $5.5 million), down from about $34 million last week. Funding is close to flat
levels: 17 to 19 November closes, the shelf that gave way on 20 November
Last week's support, now just overhead
21 November intraday low and the mid December 2025 base
scenarios: Room to retest $0.081, then the 20 day average near $0.087
Sideways while the whole market stays in Extreme Fear
fundamentals: 🏦 Institutions keep arriving: CapConnect+, the commercial paper platform built with Walmart, was approved as a Super Validator on 18 November (CIP-0131, weight up to 5). Talos, Marex and Broadridge announced a planned workflow to finance DTCC-tokenized US Treasuries on Canton Network, outside normal trading hours (planned, not live yet). A new validator application batch (objections until 25 November) includes Kiwoom Securities, CSDBR and Circle Internet Group.

🔥 Burn vs mint: CIP-0132, proposed on 16 November by Digital Asset, is the first technical plan for universal burn: dedicated synchronizers would pay for their traffic by burning CC on the Global Synchronizer. Burning is still behind minting: supply grew from 40.06 to 40.10 billion CC this week, and reports citing CantonScan put the daily burn at about 80% of the daily mint. Total CC burned passed 6.13 billion (16 November).

🧾 Tokenized shares: Fairmint announced plans on 20 November for Fairmint TSV, a venue for issuer-sponsored tokenized shares on Canton with Tradecraft as its first market maker. It has not started trading yet, and access will be permissioned.

🧰 Grants and tools: new development fund proposals were filed this week, including 9.5 million CC for on-chain enforcement of Super Validator and app locking (Digital Asset and Obsidian Systems), 2.4 million CC for a public asset data feed (Fairmint with Blockworks) and 4.8 million CC for multi-synchronizer developer tools (BitDynamics). Digital Asset published an update on covalidation, now used by Loop, T-RIZE and Bron. No unlocks, ETF filings or new spot listings found.
cntn_table: About $98 million (81.1 million shares, 30 Sep count)
cntn_notes: CNTN is Canton Strategic Holdings, a Nasdaq company that holds Canton Coin. It is not Digital Asset, the private company that built Canton Network.

Third quarter results (16 November): revenue of about $3.05 million, double the second quarter, and the company's first positive adjusted EBITDA (about $0.61 million). The net loss was about $35.1 million. It reported holding about 3.83 billion CC and about $26.9 million in cash on 30 September.

Tokenized CNTN: shares have traded on TSV LLC since 4 November, for verified participants only. Fairmint's separate new venue, Fairmint TSV, is announced but not trading. South African access has not been announced.
You can buy CNTN through Interactive Brokers from most countries, or any US broker. See the step-by-step guide.
bottom_line: 📉 CC slipped below last week's $0.075 support and sits near $0.071, its lowest since December 2025, while the whole market stays in Extreme Fear.
🏦 The institutional list keeps growing (CapConnect+, Talos, Marex, Broadridge) and the burn plan got its first technical spec, but supply still grows week by week.
👀 Selling volume is fading and RSI is near 30. A daily close back above $0.075 would be the first sign of repair; below $0.071, the December lows come into view.
